verses.text: Listen to what the LORD says: “Stand up and plead your case before the mountains. Let the hills hear your voice.
“Hear the LORD’s case, you mountains, and you enduring foundations of the earth. The LORD has a case against his people; he is bringing charges against Israel.
“My people, what have I done to you? How have I worn you out? Answer me!
“I brought you out of Egypt and freed you from slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead you.
“My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned and how Balaam son of Beor answered him—from Shittim to Gilgal—so you may know the LORD’s righteous acts.”
What should I bring when I come before the LORD and bow before God on high? Should I bring burnt offerings, year-old calves?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams or rivers of oil without number? Should I give my firstborn for my rebellion, the child of my body for my own sin?
He has already shown you what is good. What does the LORD ask of you? Do what is right, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God.
The LORD’s voice calls to the city—and wisdom reveres your name: “Pay attention to the rod and to the one who appointed it.
“Are dishonest treasures still in the wicked person’s house, along with a cursed, undersized measure?
“Can I tolerate dishonest scales and a bag of rigged weights?
“The rich are full of violence. The people speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful.
“So I have struck you with a painful wound and made you desolate because of your sins.
“You will eat but never feel satisfied; your hunger will remain. You will save things, but won’t keep them. Whatever you do save, I will hand over to the sword.
“You will plant but not harvest. You will press olives but won’t have oil to rub on yourself; you will crush grapes but won’t drink the wine.
“You have kept Omri’s rules and followed everything Ahab’s family did. You live by their advice, so I will make you a ruin, your people an object of scorn, and you will bear my people’s reproach.”
